# Testability & Acceptance Criteria Checklist: Application Logging and Observability

**Purpose**: Validate that the acceptance scenarios and success criteria are measurable,
unambiguous, and objectively verifiable before implementation.
**Created**: 2026-08-24
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Measurability of Success Criteria

- [ ] CHK001 Is SC-001's "100% of handled requests produce a request log entry" bounded to a defined request scope (which paths/methods count) so it is objectively measurable? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK002 Are the fields whose presence must be asserted per entry (timestamp, level, correlation id) enumerated so SC-002 is objectively checkable? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK003 Is "filterable by level" (SC-002) expressed with an observable pass/fail outcome (only entries at/above the selected level appear)? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK004 Is the "representative sample of activity" in SC-004 defined precisely (size and selection) so the 0-secrets criterion is verifiable? [Ambiguity, Spec §SC-004]
- [ ] CHK005 Is SC-005's "changing one configuration value changes the level" stated with an unambiguous before/after outcome? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005]

## Acceptance Scenario Quality

- [ ] CHK006 Do the US1 acceptance scenarios specify the exact fields to assert (method, path, status, duration) rather than "enough context"? [Clarity, Spec §US1]
- [ ] CHK007 Is "enough context to locate the cause" (US1 scenario 2) given a concrete field set or measurable definition? [Ambiguity, Spec §US1]
- [ ] CHK008 Are the US4 verbosity acceptance scenarios stated as concrete level thresholds (which levels appear at which setting)? [Measurability, Spec §US4]
- [ ] CHK009 Are acceptance criteria for the correlation-id reuse-vs-generate branch defined so both paths are independently verifiable? [Coverage, Spec §FR-004]

## Threshold & Metric Definition

- [ ] CHK010 Is a measurable bound defined for logging overhead/performance, or is its absence explicitly acknowledged? [Gap, Non-Functional]
- [ ] CHK011 Is the set of secret categories (authorization, cookie, tokens, session ids) enumerated so SC-004's 0-count is objectively testable? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004]
- [ ] CHK012 Is "personal family-member content" defined as an enumerable field set so its absence in logs can be objectively asserted? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007]

## Scenario-Class Verifiability

- [ ] CHK013 Are acceptance criteria for the error path (error logged AND server keeps serving) given an observable "still serving" check? [Coverage, Spec §SC-006]
- [ ] CHK014 Are measurable criteria defined for the "logging failure does not crash the app" resilience requirement? [Measurability, Spec §FR-010]

## Documentation & Traceability

- [ ] CHK015 Is SC-007 ("operator can determine from docs") given an objective completeness criterion (which items must be documented)? [Measurability, Spec §SC-007]
- [ ] CHK016 Does every success criterion (SC-001..SC-007) map to at least one functional requirement so acceptance is traceable? [Traceability]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Lens: Testability & acceptance criteria | Depth: Standard (PR review) | Audience: Reviewer
- Complements the broader `logging.md` checklist (does not duplicate its completeness/consistency items)
